data.overview: Standard reduced-k renormalization exaggerates the cost of using fewer experts. An interior reference set restores most downstream quality, whereas both k2=k1 and k2=E can be harmful. Perplexity and MMLU prefer different k2 on the 35B model.

key_results.interpretation: halves routed-expert compute with no statistically detectable loss (p=0.66).

key_results.interpretation: 50% routed-expert compute reduction, 44% expert-term reduction, estimated 17% end-to-end active-parameter reduction.

negative_results.name: Perplexity mis-ranks k2
negative_results.description: 35B PPL prefers k2=8 while MMLU prefers k2=16; k2=8 is significantly -1.10 MMLU points (p=0.021).

negative_results.name: No memory saving
negative_results.description: all E experts remain resident; method only reduces executed expert compute and related weight traffic.

negative_results.name: Same-series evidence
negative_results.description: two main models are Qwen family; cross-architecture generalization remains hypothesis.

negative_results.name: Coarse router boundary
negative_results.description: mechanism predicts smaller benefit when top-k mass is less flat; Gemma top-8 mass 0.302 shows weaker normalization sensitivity.

data.interpretation: Gain calibration is a hidden confounder in post-training k reduction. Expert identity matters substantially more than precise weighting, enabling a cheap amplitude correction while preserving exact router ranking.
data.quality_impact: Selected k2 recovers most downstream quality, but exact equivalence is not shown and k2 should be validated on downstream tasks.
